question: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) receivers can provide a reference clock signal known as Pulse-per-Second (PPS or 1-PPS). Is the PPS physically generated through a digitally-controlled oscillator (or line driver) whose offset is periodically re-initialized by the estimated clock bias (retrieved by means of PVT algorithms)?

sections.title: PPS Generation and Hardware Implementation
sections.text: In various experimental setups, the Pulse-per-Second signal is produced by distinct hardware components depending on the side of the communication link. On the receiving end, the PPS signal can be generated directly by a GNSS RTK receiver, such as the GINTEC M1G2 model [1]. Conversely, on the transmitting side, a reference PPS signal may be derived from a GPS-disciplined rubidium oscillator, specifically the Quartzlock E80, to ensure synchronization [1]. These implementations demonstrate that while the source of the timing reference varies, the PPS serves as the fundamental synchronization marker for the system.

snippets: To ensure full synchronization of transmitting and receiving, a reference PPS (Pulse Per Second) signal was used, generated on the transmitting side by the Quartzlock E80-GPS disciplined rubidium oscillator (whose starting point is synchronized with the beginning of the UTC second)
while on the receiving side, the PPS signal was generated by the GNSS RTK Receiver GINTEC M1G2.

sections.title: Oscillator Discipline and Phase Dynamics
sections.text: The physical generation of the PPS is closely linked to the behavior of the underlying oscillator. In systems utilizing an FPGA-based GPS-disciplined oscillator, the output frequency is mathematically consistent with the time derivative of the 1PPS phase [2]. This relationship indicates that the oscillator's frequency is controlled to maintain a specific phase relationship with the reference signal, rather than being a simple digital toggle. The discipline mechanism ensures that the local oscillator remains aligned with the satellite-derived time standard, effectively managing the phase error over time.

snippets: The derivative of the 1PPS phase in time is consistent with the output frequency.
citations.title: fpga-based autonomous gps-disciplined oscillatorsfor wireless sensor network nodes

sections.title: Timing Accuracy and Bias Correction
sections.text: The PPS signal provided by standard GPS receivers is not perfectly aligned with the true GPS second, exhibiting an offset of up to 50 nanoseconds [3]. To address this discrepancy, the receiver provides a periodic correction for this offset [3]. This process implies that the raw PPS output contains a bias that must be estimated and adjusted. The correction mechanism suggests that the receiver's internal timing is periodically re-initialized or adjusted based on the estimated clock bias, ensuring that the final time reference meets the required precision standards for scientific applications.

snippets: The GPS 1 PPS signal is offset from the true GPS second by up to $50\mathrm{ns}$ , and a correction for this offset is provided periodically by the receiver.

sections.title: Application in Measurement Timestamping
sections.text: The primary utility of the PPS signal in research contexts is the precise timestamping of data. Embedded microcontrollers utilize the 1PPS signal to timestamp measurements relative to the beginning of a whole second [4]. This capability allows for the correlation of local sensor data with a global time reference. By anchoring measurement times to the PPS edge, systems can achieve high-precision temporal alignment, which is critical for applications requiring synchronization between distributed nodes or between local sensors and satellite time standards.

snippets: The embedded microcontroller can then timestamp measurements relative the beginning of a whole second.

question: During pre-training, why is the transformer embedding layer initialized randomly, rather than with pre-trained embeddings from existing models?

sections.title: Initialization Options and Experimental Configurations
sections.text: The initialization of the transformer embedding layer during pre-training is not a singular fixed practice but rather a choice between distinct strategies. Researchers have identified that the embedding layer can be set up with random values or seeded with existing representations from models like word2vec or GloVe [2]. To evaluate the impact of these choices, experimental designs often compare two specific configurations: one where the layer is initialized randomly and updated during training, and another where it is initialized with pre-trained representations and subsequently updated [1]. This comparative approach allows for the isolation of the initialization method as a variable in the training process [1].

snippets: We perform experiments with two configurations of the embedding layer: (1) Random, initialized randomly and updated during training, and (2) Pre-trained, initialized by pre-trained representations and updated during training.
citations.title: towards a seamless integration of word senses into downstream nlp applications

snippets: Prior to training, the embedding layer can be initialized randomly, or initialized by pre-trained embeddings like word2vec [19] or GloVe [21]

sections.title: Rationale for Using Pre-trained Embeddings
sections.text: The primary motivation for utilizing pre-trained word embeddings is to enhance the model's ability to extract comprehensive information, particularly when working with smaller datasets [3]. By leveraging existing knowledge encoded in these representations, deep learning models can potentially achieve better performance with less data [3]. This approach is often employed to facilitate the learning process by providing a strong initial semantic foundation for the model [3].

snippets: At embedding layer, deep learning models make use of pre-trained word embeddings that facilitate them to extract more comprehensive information even from smaller datasets [51].

While training deep learning models, pre-trained word embeddings only facilitate models with pre-trained weights at only embedding layer, other layers of model are still initialized with random weights.
citations.title: passion-net: a robust precise and explainable predictor for hate speech detection in roman urdu text

sections.title: Limitations of Partial Pre-training
sections.text: However, the benefits of pre-trained embeddings are limited to the specific layer where they are applied. While the embedding layer may contain pre-trained weights, the remaining layers of the model are still initialized with random weights [3]. This means that the rest of the network must still learn its parameters from scratch, which can create a mismatch or require additional training steps to align the pre-trained embeddings with the randomly initialized higher layers [3]. Consequently, the advantage of pre-trained embeddings is confined to the input representation stage rather than the entire model architecture [3].

snippets: At embedding layer, deep learning models make use of pre-trained word embeddings that facilitate them to extract more comprehensive information even from smaller datasets [51].

While training deep learning models, pre-trained word embeddings only facilitate models with pre-trained weights at only embedding layer, other layers of model are still initialized with random weights.

sections.title: Training from Scratch with Context-independent Embeddings
sections.text: In certain model architectures, such as the TK, TKL, and CK models, the training process begins entirely from scratch [4]. In these cases, the embedding layer is initialized using context-independent embeddings rather than random noise or context-aware pre-trained vectors [4]. This approach emphasizes a complete learning process where all components, including the embedding layer, are derived from the training data without reliance on external pre-trained resources [4]. The explicit mention of training 'from scratch' highlights that random or context-independent initialization is a valid and utilized strategy in specific transformer-based systems [4].

snippets: The TK, TKL, and CK models are trained from scratch (yes, from scratch) with an embedding layer initialized using context-independent embeddings.

sections.title: Research Context and Sources
sections.text: The discussion on embedding initialization is supported by recent literature, including the DEPT framework from 2024 and the AMMUS survey from 2021. These sources provide the foundational context for understanding the mechanisms and design rationales behind embedding layer initialization in pre-trained language models. The question of why random initialization is often preferred over pre-trained embeddings remains a key area of inquiry in this domain.
